holidays.name: National Animal Cracker Day
holidays.description: Grab a handful of tiny lions, tigers, and elephants and snack on the whole zoo. Today is for crunching the cookie menagerie, one head at a time. Bonus points if you pretend your lion is escaping before you bite it.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial snack observance, and nobody has pinned down who started it. It honors the animal-shaped crackers that became popular in the early 1900s.
holidays.funFact: Barnum's Animal Crackers first appeared in 1902. The circus-wagon box with a string handle was designed so it could hang from a Christmas tree.

holidays.name: National Velociraptor Awareness Day
holidays.description: A day to think about the small, clever, and very toothy dinosaur. Spend it reading up on raptors, watching a certain dino-filled movie, or making sure all your doors have working latches.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial pop-culture and science observance, and its origin is unclear. It celebrates the dromaeosaurid dinosaur that became a movie star.
holidays.funFact: Real Velociraptors were roughly the size of a turkey and were covered in feathers. That's quite different from the large, scaly ones in the movies.

holidays.name: Pet Owners Independence Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek day when pet owners take a break from walks, feedings, and litter duty. You can imagine your pets doing their own chores while you relax. The pets will probably not agree.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin, kept up by pet lovers who enjoy poking fun at who is really in charge at home.
holidays.funFact: Plenty of cat and dog owners suspect their pets run the household, and this day lets them joke about it.
